sanskrit: damayann iva damyānāṃ śaśvad bhāraṃ pravardhayet mṛdupūrvaṃ prayatnena pāśān abhyavahārayet
english: As one who tames steeds yet to be broken, let him steadily increase their burden, and gently, with patient effort, draw the harness over them.

sanskrit: sakṛt pāśāvakīrṇās te na bhaviṣyanti durdamāḥ ucitenaiva bhoktavyās te bhaviṣyanti yatnataḥ
english: Once entangled in the harness, they will no longer be hard to govern; treated as is fitting, with care, they will become amenable.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvasamārambho durlabhaḥ puruṣavrajaḥ yathāmukhyān sāntvayitvā bhoktavya itaro janaḥ
english: Therefore, since a throng of men is hard to set in motion all at once, having first conciliated the chief among them, let him then draw revenue from the rest of the people.

sanskrit: tatas tān bhedayitvātha parasparavivakṣitān bhuñjīta sāntvayitvaiva yathāsukham ayatnataḥ
english: Then, having set at variance those inclined to dispute among themselves, and having won them over, let him draw upon them at ease, without strain.

sanskrit: na cāsthāne na cākāle karān ebhyo 'nupātayet ānupūrvyeṇa sāntvena yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi
english: Let him not levy taxes upon them in the wrong place or at the wrong time, but in due order, with gentleness, at the proper season, and according to rule.

sanskrit: upāyān prabravīmy etān na me māyā vivakṣitā anupāyena damayan prakopayati vājinaḥ
english: These I declare to be skillful means; no deceit is what I intend. He who tames by the wrong means only provokes his horses to fury.

sanskrit: pānāgārāṇi veśāś ca veśaprāpaṇikās tathā kuśīlavāḥ sakitavā ye cānye ke cid īdṛśāḥ
english: Drinking-houses and brothels, and those who keep procuresses, actors and gamblers, and whatever others are of this kind—

sanskrit: niyamyāḥ sarva evaite ye rāṣṭrasyopaghātakāḥ ete rāṣṭre hi tiṣṭhanto bādhante bhadrikāḥ prajāḥ
english: all these must be restrained, for they are the bane of the realm; abiding within it, they oppress the honest folk.

sanskrit: na kena cid yācitavyaḥ kaś cit kiṃ cid anāpadi iti vyavasthā bhūtānāṃ purastān manunā kṛtā
english: "By no one shall anything be begged of another save in distress"—such was the ordinance laid down of old for all beings by Manu.

sanskrit: sarve tathā na jīveyur na kuryuḥ karma ced iha sarva eva trayo lokā na bhaveyur asaṃśayam
english: For if all men were to live thus and did no labor here, then without doubt all the three worlds would cease to be.

sanskrit: prabhur niyamane rājā ya etān na niyacchati bhuṅkte sa tasya pāpasya caturbhāgam iti śrutiḥ tathā kṛtasya dharmasya caturbhāgam upāśnute
english: The king is master to restrain them; he who does not restrain such men shares a fourth part of their guilt, so says the sacred lore—just as, when righteousness is done, he partakes of a fourth part of its merit.

sanskrit: sthānāny etāni saṃgamya prasaṅge bhūtināśanaḥ kāmaprasaktaḥ puruṣaḥ kim akāryaṃ vivarjayet
english: Frequenting these haunts and given over to their allure, a man bent on his welfare's ruin, enslaved to desire—what wicked deed would he forbear?

sanskrit: āpady eva tu yāceran yeṣāṃ nāsti parigrahaḥ dātavyaṃ dharmatas tebhyas tv anukrośād dayārthinā
english: Yet in distress alone may those who have no possessions beg; to them gift should be made righteously, out of compassion, by one who is moved to mercy.

sanskrit: mā te rāṣṭre yācanakā mā te bhūyuś ca dasyavaḥ iṣṭādātāra evaite naite bhūtasya bhāvakāḥ
english: Let there be no beggars in your realm, and let there be no robbers; both alike are mere takers of what is desired, neither of them nurturers of living beings.

sanskrit: ye bhūtāny anugṛhṇanti vardhayanti ca ye prajāḥ te te rāṣṭre pravartantāṃ mā bhūtānām abhāvakāḥ
english: Those who favor living beings and those who make the people thrive—let such men flourish in your realm, and not those who fail to nurture creatures.

sanskrit: daṇḍyās te ca mahārāja dhanādānaprayojanāḥ prayogaṃ kārayeyus tān yathā balikarāṃs tathā
english: And those whose aim is to seize wealth deserve punishment, O great king; let him set them to honest occupation, even as he sets tribute-payers to theirs.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ yac cānyat kiṃ cid īdṛśam puruṣaiḥ kārayet karma bahubhiḥ saha karmibhiḥ
english: Agriculture, cattle-keeping, and trade, and whatever else is of this kind—let him have such work done by men together with many laborers.

sanskrit: naraś cet kṛṣigorakṣyaṃ vāṇijyaṃ cāpy anuṣṭhitaḥ saṃśayaṃ labhate kiṃ cit tena rājā vigarhyate
english: If a man engaged in farming, cattle-rearing, or trade should fall into any peril through it, the king is held blameworthy.

sanskrit: dhaninaḥ pūjayen nityaṃ yānācchādanabhojanaiḥ vaktavyāś cānugṛhṇīdhvaṃ pūjāḥ saha mayeti ha
english: Let him always honor the wealthy with carriages, raiment, and food, and they should be told: "Receive these honors along with me."

sanskrit: aṅgam etan mahad rājñāṃ dhanino nāma bhārata kakudaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dhanastho nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: This is a mighty limb of kings—the wealthy man, O Bhārata; the man of means is the very summit of all beings, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: prājñaḥ śūro dhanasthaś ca svām dhārmika eva ca tapasvī satyavādī ca buddhimāṃś cābhirakṣati
english: The wise man, the hero, the man of wealth, the righteous, the ascetic, the truthful, and the man of understanding—each guards his own.

sanskrit: tasmād eteṣu sarveṣu prītimān bhava pārthiva satyam ārjavam akrodham ānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca pālaya
english: Therefore be well-disposed toward all of these, O prince, and uphold truth, uprightness, freedom from wrath, and absence of cruelty.

sanskrit: evaṃ daṇḍaṃ ca kośaṃ ca mitraṃ bhūmiṃ ca lapsyase satyārjavaparo rājan mitrakośasamanvitaḥ
english: Thus shall you gain the power to punish, a treasury, allies, and land; devoted to truth and uprightness, O king, you will be furnished with friends and treasure.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vanaspatīn bhakṣyaphalān na chindyur viṣaye tava brāhmaṇānāṃ mūlaphalaṃ dharmyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Let them not fell, within your domain, trees that bear edible fruit; for the wise declare that roots and fruit are the rightful portion of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyo 'tiriktaṃ ca bhuñjīrann itare janāḥ na brāhmaṇoparodhena hared anyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Let other folk consume only what is left over after the brāhmaṇas; never may another take so as to deprive a brāhmaṇa in any way.

sanskrit: vipraś cet tyāgam ātiṣṭhed ākhyāyāvṛttikarśitaḥ parikalpyāsya vṛttiḥ syāt sadārasya narādhipa
english: If a brāhmaṇa, worn thin by want of livelihood, should make this known and take to renunciation, a means of support should be provided for him together with his wife, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sa cen nopanivarteta vācyo brāhmaṇasaṃsadi kasminn idānīṃ maryādām ayaṃ lokaḥ kariṣyati
english: If he does not turn back from it, he is to be admonished in the assembly of brāhmaṇas: "In whom, then, will this world now find its bound of right conduct?"

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ nivarteta na ced vakṣyaty ataḥ param pūrvaṃ parokṣaṃ kartavyam etat kaunteya śāsanam
english: Without doubt he will desist, if he says nothing further; but this correction, O son of Kuntī, should first be done out of his hearing.

sanskrit: āhur etaj janā brahman na caitac chraddadhāmy aham nimantryaś ca bhaved bhogair avṛttyā cet tadācaret
english: "People say this, O brahman, yet I do not put faith in it; and he should be won over with enjoyments, should he act so for want of livelihood."

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ lokānām iha jīvanam ūrdhvaṃ caiva trayī vidyā sā bhūtān bhāvayaty uta
english: Agriculture, cattle-keeping, and trade are the livelihood of folk here below; and higher still is the threefold lore—it is that which sustains all beings.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ prayatamānāyāṃ ye syus tatparipanthinaḥ dasyavas tadvadhāyeha brahmā kṣatram athāsṛjat
english: When that lore is being striven after, those who become its adversaries are robbers; for their slaying here below, Brahmā then created the warrior order.

sanskrit: śatrūñ jahi prajā rakṣa yajasva kratubhir nṛpa yudhyasva samare vīro bhūtvā kauravanandana
english: Slay your foes, protect the people, perform the sacrifices, O king; fight in battle, having become a hero, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyān pālayed rājā yaḥ sa rājāryakṛttamaḥ ye ke cit tān na rakṣanti tair artho nāsti kaś cana
english: The king who guards those to be protected is the noblest doer of kingly deeds; whoever fail to protect them are of no use whatever.

sanskrit: sadaiva rājñā boddhavyaṃ sarvalokād yudhiṣṭhira tasmād dhetor hi bhuñjīta manuṣyān eva mānavaḥ
english: Ever must the king keep watch over all the people, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for that very reason should the ruler of men draw his sustenance from men.

sanskrit: antarebhyaḥ parān rakṣan parebhyaḥ punar antarān parān parebhyaḥ svān svebhyaḥ sarvān pālaya nityadā
english: Guarding outsiders from those within, and again those within from outsiders, outsiders from outsiders and your own from your own—protect them all without ceasing.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ sarvato rakṣan rājā rakṣeta medinīm ātmamūlam idaṃ sarvam āhur hi viduṣo janāḥ
english: Guarding himself on every side, let the king guard the earth; for the learned declare that all this has its root in the self.

sanskrit: kiṃ chidraṃ ko 'nuṣaṅgo me kiṃ vāsty avinipātitam kuto mām āsraved doṣa iti nityaṃ vicintayet
english: "What is my weak point? What entanglement is mine? What lies undone? From what quarter may some flaw flow in upon me?"—thus let him reflect continually.

sanskrit: guptaiś cārair anumataiḥ pṛthivīm anucārayet sunītaṃ yadi me vṛttaṃ praśaṃsanti na vā punaḥ kaccid rocej janapade kaccid rāṣṭre ca me yaśaḥ
english: With trusted spies, well-approved, let him keep watch over the land: "Is my conduct rightly ordered—do they praise it or not? Do I find favor in the countryside? Does my fame stand bright in the realm?"

sanskrit: dharmajñānāṃ dhṛtimatāṃ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinām rāṣṭraṃ ca ye 'nujīvanti ye ca rājño 'nujīvinaḥ
english: Of those who know the law, who are steadfast, who do not flee in battle, of those who live by the realm and those who live by the king,

sanskrit: amātyānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ madhyasthānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ye ca tvābhipraśaṃseyur nindeyur atha vā punaḥ sarvān supariṇītāṃs tān kārayeta yudhiṣṭhira
english: and of all the ministers and all the neutral parties everywhere, and of those who praise you or who blame you—make them all well-governed, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ekāntena hi sarveṣāṃ na śakyaṃ tāta rocitum mitrāmitram atho madhyaṃ sarvabhūteṣu bhārata
english: For it is not possible, my son, to please all utterly; among all beings there is friend, foe, and the neutral, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tulyabāhubalānāṃ ca guṇair api niṣevinām kathaṃ syād adhikaḥ kaś cit sa tu bhuñjīta mānavān
english: Among men equal in the strength of their arms and alike attended by virtues, how should any one be superior? Yet it is he who shall draw revenue from men.

sanskrit: ye carā hy acarān adyur adaṃṣṭrān daṃṣṭriṇas tathā āśīviṣā iva kruddhā bhujagā bhujagān iva
english: For the moving devour the unmoving, and the fanged devour the fangless, like venomous serpents enraged, like snakes devouring snakes.

sanskrit: etebhyaś cāpramattaḥ syāt sadā yatto yudhiṣṭhira bhāruṇḍasadṛśā hy ete nipatanti pramādyataḥ
english: Against these be ever heedful and on guard, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for these are like the bhāruṇḍa birds—they swoop down upon the careless.

sanskrit: kaccit te vaṇijo rāṣṭre nodvijante karārditāḥ krīṇanto bahu vālpena kāntārakṛtaniśramāḥ
english: I trust the merchants in your realm are not driven to despair, afflicted by taxes—those who buy much for little and toil through the wilderness ways?

sanskrit: kaccit kṛṣikarā rāṣṭraṃ na jahaty atipīḍitāḥ ye vahanti dhuraṃ rājñāṃ saṃbharantītarān api
english: I trust the tillers, when too sorely oppressed, do not abandon the realm—they who bear the yoke for kings and sustain all the rest besides?

sanskrit: ito dattena jīvanti devāḥ pitṛgaṇās tathā manuṣyoragarakṣāṃsi vayāṃsi paśavas tathā
english: By what is given from their hands live the gods and the hosts of ancestors, men, serpents, and rākṣasas, the birds, and the beasts as well.

sanskrit: eṣā te rāṣṭravṛttiś ca rāṣṭraguptiś ca bhārata etam evārtham āśritya bhūyo vakṣyāmi pāṇḍava
english: This is the conduct of the realm for you and the safeguarding of the realm, O Bhārata; resting upon this very theme, I shall speak yet further, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yān aṅgirāḥ kṣatradharmān utathyo brahmavittamaḥ māndhātre yauvanāśvāya prītimān abhyabhāṣata
english: Bhīṣma said: Those duties of the warrior caste which Utathya, the Aṅgirasa, foremost knower of the Veda, spoke with goodwill to Māndhātṛ, the son of Yuvanāśva—

sanskrit: sa yathānuśaśāsainam utathyo brahmavittamaḥ tat te sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi nikhilena yudhiṣṭhira
english: even as Utathya, foremost knower of the Veda, instructed him, all that I shall declare to you in full, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: utathya uvāca dharmāya rājā bhavati na kāmakaraṇāya tu māndhātar evaṃ jānīhi rājā lokasya rakṣitā
english: Utathya said: A king exists for the sake of righteousness, not for the working of his own desire; know it thus, O Māndhātṛ—the king is the protector of the world.

sanskrit: rājā carati vai dharmaṃ devatvāyaiva gacchati na ced dharmaṃ sa carati narakāyaiva gacchati
english: If a king practices righteousness, he goes indeed unto godhood; but if he does not practice righteousness, he goes straight to hell.

sanskrit: dharme tiṣṭhanti bhūtāni dharmo rājani tiṣṭhati taṃ rājā sādhu yaḥ śāsti sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: Upon righteousness all beings rest; righteousness rests upon the king; the king who governs that righteousness well—he is a king, a lord of the earth.

sanskrit: rājā paramadharmātmā lakṣmīvān pāpa ucyate devāś ca garhāṃ gacchanti dharmo nāstīti cocyate
english: When a king of the highest righteous soul, endowed with fortune, is yet called wicked, then the gods too fall into reproach, and it is said, "There is no righteousness."

sanskrit: adharme vartamānānām arthasiddhiḥ pradṛśyate tad eva maṅgalaṃ sarvaṃ lokaḥ samanuvartate
english: When the prosperity of those who dwell in unrighteousness is seen, the world takes that for the whole of blessedness and follows after it.

sanskrit: ucchidyate dharmavṛttam adharmo vartate mahān bhayam āhur divārātraṃ yadā pāpo na vāryate
english: Righteous conduct is cut away, and great unrighteousness prevails; men say there is dread by day and night when the wicked man is not restrained.

sanskrit: na vedān anuvartanti vratavanto dvijātayaḥ na yajñāṃs tanvate viprā yadā pāpo na vāryate
english: The twice-born who keep their vows no longer follow the Vedas, and the brāhmaṇas spread out no sacrifices, when the wicked man is not restrained.

sanskrit: vadhyānām iva sarveṣāṃ mano bhavati vihvalam manuṣyāṇāṃ mahārāja yadā pāpo na vāryate
english: The minds of all men grow distraught, as of those condemned to death, O great king, when the wicked man is not restrained.

sanskrit: ubhau lokāv abhiprekṣya rājānam ṛṣayaḥ svayam asṛjan sumahad bhūtam ayaṃ dharmo bhaviṣyati
english: Looking to both worlds, the seers themselves brought forth the king, that mighty being: "This shall be righteousness incarnate."

sanskrit: yasmin dharmo virājeta taṃ rājānaṃ pracakṣate yasmin vilīyate dharmas taṃ devā vṛṣalaṃ viduḥ
english: In whom righteousness shines forth, him they proclaim a king; in whom righteousness dissolves away, him the gods know for a base outcaste.

sanskrit: vṛṣo hi bhagavān dharmo yas tasya kurute hy alam vṛṣalaṃ taṃ vidur devās tasmād dharmaṃ na lopayet
english: For the blessed Dharma is the Bull; whoever cuts that Bull short, him the gods know as the bull-mangler, the outcaste—therefore let none destroy righteousness.

sanskrit: dharme vardhati vardhanti sarvabhūtāni sarvadā tasmin hrasati hīyante tasmād dharmaṃ pravardhayet
english: When righteousness waxes, all beings ever wax with it; when it wanes, they wane away—therefore let him cause righteousness to flourish.

sanskrit: dhanāt sravati dharmo hi dhāraṇād veti niścayaḥ akāryāṇāṃ manuṣyendra sa sīmāntakaraḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Righteousness flows from wealth, or else, it is held, from sustaining; it is remembered, O lord of men, as the setter of the bound against forbidden deeds.

sanskrit: prabhavārthaṃ hi bhūtānāṃ dharmaḥ sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā tasmāt pravardhayed dharmaṃ prajānugrahakāraṇāt
english: For the welfare of beings was righteousness created by the Self-existent; therefore let him make righteousness flourish, for the sake of grace toward the people.

sanskrit: tasmād dhi rājaśārdūla dharmaḥ śreṣṭha iti smṛtaḥ sa rājā yaḥ prajāḥ śāsti sādhukṛt puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: For that reason, O tiger among kings, righteousness is remembered as supreme; he is a king who governs the people, a doer of good, a bull among men.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhāv anādṛtya dharmam evānupālayet dharmaḥ śreyaskaratamo rājñāṃ bharatasattama
english: Disregarding desire and wrath, let him uphold righteousness alone; righteousness is the surest bringer of welfare to kings, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dharmasya brāhmaṇā yonis tasmāt tān pūjayet sadā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca māndhātaḥ kāmān kuryād amatsarī
english: The brāhmaṇas are the womb of righteousness; therefore let him ever honor them, and let him, free of grudging, O Māndhātṛ, fulfill the desires of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hy akāmakaraṇād rājñaḥ saṃjāyate bhayam mitrāṇi ca na vardhante tathāmitrībhavanty api
english: For from not fulfilling their desires there arises danger to the king; his friends increase not, and they even turn to enemies.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān vai tadāsūyād yadā vairocano baliḥ athāsmāc chrīr apākrāmad yāsminn āsīt pratāpinī
english: When Bali, son of Virocana, came to bear ill will toward the brāhmaṇas, then majestic Fortune, who had dwelt in him, departed from him.

sanskrit: tatas tasmād apakramya sāgacchat pākaśāsanam atha so 'nvatapat paścāc chriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā puraṃdare
english: Then, having gone forth from him, she passed to Indra, the chastiser of Pāka; and afterward Bali grieved sorely, beholding Fortune now in Purandara.

sanskrit: etat phalam asūyāyā abhimānasya cābhibho tasmād budhyasva māndhātar mā tvā jahyāt pratāpinī
english: This is the fruit of envy and of pride, O mighty one; therefore take heed, O Māndhātṛ, lest majestic Fortune forsake you.

sanskrit: darpo nāma śriyaḥ putro jajñe 'dharmād iti śrutiḥ tena devāsurā rājan nītāḥ subahuśo vaśam
english: Insolence by name, the son of Fortune, was born of unrighteousness, so says the sacred lore; by him, O king, gods and asuras alike were again and again brought under sway.

sanskrit: rājarṣayaś ca bahavas tasmād budhyasva pārthiva rājā bhavati taṃ jitvā dāsas tena parājitaḥ
english: And many royal seers as well; therefore take heed, O prince. Conquering him, one becomes a king; vanquished by him, one becomes a slave.

sanskrit: sa yathā darpasahitam adharmaṃ nānusevase tathā vartasva māndhātaś ciraṃ cet sthātum icchasi
english: So conduct yourself, O Māndhātṛ, that you cleave not to unrighteousness joined with insolence, if you wish to endure for long.

sanskrit: mattāt pramattāt pogaṇḍād unmattāc ca viśeṣataḥ tadabhyāsād upāvartād ahitānāṃ ca sevanāt
english: From the drunken, the heedless, the half-grown boy, and above all from the madman, from the practice of their ways, from association with them, and from the company of the ill-disposed—

sanskrit: nigṛhītād amātyāc ca strībhyaś caiva viśeṣataḥ parvatād viṣamād durgād dhastino 'śvāt sarīsṛpāt
english: from a minister who has been disgraced, and above all from women, from mountain and ravine and fastness, from elephant, horse, and creeping thing—

sanskrit: etebhyo nityayattaḥ syān naktaṃcaryāṃ ca varjayet atyāyaṃ cātimānaṃ ca dambhaṃ krodhaṃ ca varjayet
english: against all these let him be ever on guard, and let him shun roaming by night; let him shun excessive spending, overweening pride, hypocrisy, and wrath.

sanskrit: avijñātāsu ca strīṣu klībāsu svairiṇīṣu ca parabhāryāsu kanyāsu nācaren maithunaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: With women unknown to him, with the unsexed, with wanton women, with the wives of others, and with maidens, let the king not engage in union.

sanskrit: kuleṣu pāparakṣāṃsi jāyante varṇasaṃkarāt apumāṃso 'ṅgahīnāś ca sthūlajihvā vicetasaḥ
english: From the confusion of castes there are born into families wicked, demon-like beings—the unmanly, the maimed of limb, the thick-tongued, and the witless.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca jāyante yadā rājā pramādyati tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa vartitavyaṃ prajāhite
english: These and others are born when the king grows negligent; therefore the king must conduct himself with especial care for the welfare of the people.
